newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Vierfontein rises on restructuring talks.
newsitem.headline: Vierfontein rises on restructuring talks.

text.p: Shares in South African coal firm Vierfontein Colliery Ltd (VCL) on Monday bucked the market's weaker trend to climb higher after the firm announced restructuring talks were continuing, dealers said.
Vierfontein was one of the few shares firming in a soggy market wailing Wall Steet's nearly 250-point slide on Friday.
By about 0830 GMT the stock was up 6.25 percent or four cents to 68 cents, making it the highest percentage gainer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE).
But volumes on the share were thin with only 11,100 shares changing hands.
"I think guys are getting on the stock on the news that the mine could be reversed into a new business and that's why the share is up while the whole market is down," one dealer said.
Viervontein said earlier on Monday that the talks, first announced in June, concerning a possible restructuring were continuing.
The company said on June 2 that Ben Nevis Holdings Ltd had approached it with proposals which could result in a new business being placed in VCL.
VCL was established to produce bituminous coal under contract from electricity utitility Eskom's Vierfontein power station in the Viljoenkroon district. It ceased production at the end of March 1988.
The contract with Eskom ended in December, 1988.
